title: Unramified morphisms detected by geometric fibre tangent spaces
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then $f$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] if and only if the following holds: for every geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], and every $\Omega$-point $x$ of $X_{\bar s}=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-pc-fibre-product], the tangent space $T_{X_{\bar s}/\Omega,x}$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] is zero. Equivalently, the only morphism of $\Omega$-schemes $\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to X_{\bar s}$ reducing to $x$ is the constant one [def-sc-dual-numbers]. Empty fibres satisfy the condition. No flatness or Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0B2G (lemma-injective-tangent-spaces-unramified), applied over an algebraically closed field; morphisms.tex Tags 02GF (lemma-unramified-at-point), 02G5 (lemma-unramified-omega-zero), and 02G8 (lemma-unramified-etale-fibres) give the fibrewise/global test. This is a geometric-point criterion, not merely a criterion at rational closed points on the original base.

proof.text: Fix $\Omega,s,x$ as in the statement and write $p:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], $p$ is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-point-tangent-unramified] to its section $x$: its image is closed with residue field $\Omega$, and $T_{X_s/\Omega,x}=0$ if and only if $p$ is unramified at that image. Thus the tangent condition at each test point is precisely the local condition in [lem-sfb-unramified-geometric-point-test].

source.place: Tag 0B2G (lemma-injective-tangent-spaces-unramified), applied to each geometric fibre structure morphism

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-unramified-geometric-point-test], the collection of local conditions in Step 1 is equivalent to $f$ being unramified. In the reverse implication that lemma tests each $z\in X$ using an algebraic closure of $\kappa(z)$; the resulting geometric point of $S$ is included in our quantifier even if its field is transcendental over $\kappa(f(z))$. This gives both implications for every source point.

At each test section the residue-field identification in [lem-sfb-rational-point-tangent-unramified] and [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space, def-sc-dual-numbers] identify tangent vectors with the relative $\Omega$-dual-number lifts of $x$. Scalar multiplication by zero precomposes with $\epsilon\mapsto0$, which factors through $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and then $x$, so the zero vector is the constant lift. A vector space is zero exactly when every vector equals its zero vector. This proves the dual-number formulation. Empty fibres have no test sections and impose no condition. For empty $X$ all conditions are vacuous, and the affine-cover formulation of [def-weil-unramified-morphism] likewise makes $f$ unramified.

source.place: Tag 0B29 (definition-dual-numbers) and Tag 0B2C (definition-tangent-space); zero scalar in the vector-space operations of Tag 0B2B

proof_origin.place: Tags 0B2E, 0B2F, 0B2G specialized to rational points in a geometric fibre, combined with morphisms.tex Tag 0475 to test at every source point via an algebraic closure of its residue field.
